Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital payment systems.  21 variables in 4 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether the instant payment system enables or plans to enable instant payments across national borders to other countries or regional payment systems, supporting remittances, trade, and regional integration.
Comments: Muni Dinero’s official app description states users can send/receive money from the CEMAC region and “other countries around the world (Spain, France, Germany, UK, USA, etc.)” ([Google Play – Muni Dinero](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.munidinero.subscriber.prod&hl=en_US)). World Bank also notes CEMAC cross-border payments exist via GIMAC/SYSTAC and interoperability phase 2 for e-money/transfers is ongoing ([World Bank Digital Economy Diagnostic PDF](https://thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/61714f214ed04bcd6e9623ad0e215897-0400012021/related/P1793391f4a4c800219f0014c68aefed3c8.pdf)). This supports partially functional cross-border capability.

Definition: Whether the system enables citizen payments to government for taxes, fees, licenses, fines, utility bills, and other government service charges.
Comments: World Bank explicitly states government payments are largely manual and there is no G2P/P2G digitization strategy in Equatorial Guinea ([World Bank Digital Economy Diagnostic PDF](https://thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/61714f214ed04bcd6e9623ad0e215897-0400012021/related/P1793391f4a4c800219f0014c68aefed3c8.pdf)). I did not find evidence of citizens paying taxes/fees digitally to government at scale.

Definition: Whether the instant payment system supports direct person-to-person transfer of funds between individuals for informal transactions, remittances, and interpersonal value transfers.
Comments: Muni Dinero’s official app description states users can “send and receive money” via its digital wallet and send/receive money from Equatorial Guinea and the CEMAC region, supporting P2P transfers ([Google Play – Muni Dinero](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.munidinero.subscriber.prod&hl=en_US)). World Bank also categorizes first-generation DFS (cash-in/out and P2P) as nascent but present after mid‑2023 licensing ([World Bank Digital Economy Diagnostic PDF](https://thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/61714f214ed04bcd6e9623ad0e215897-0400012021/related/P1793391f4a4c800219f0014c68aefed3c8.pdf)).

Definition: Whether and how the central bank participates in payment system governance beyond its regulatory oversight role, including board representation, operational management, technical standard-setting, or direct system operation.
Comments: World Bank describes BEAC as the regional central bank overseeing payments in CEMAC and managing/operating key payment systems (SYGMA RTGS; SYSTAC retail clearing) and issuing instructions on interoperability ([World Bank Digital Economy Diagnostic PDF](https://thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/61714f214ed04bcd6e9623ad0e215897-0400012021/related/P1793391f4a4c800219f0014c68aefed3c8.pdf)). BEAC’s official site lists its mission includes “promouvoir le bon fonctionnement des systèmes de paiement et de règlement” ([BEAC – La BEAC](https://www.beac.int/beac/la-beac/)). This indicates direct operation at least at the regional level that covers Equatorial Guinea.

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital payment systems.  21 variables in 4 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing an instant/real-time payment system (IPS/RTP) that enables digital payments with near-instant settlement (typically within seconds), available 24/7/365. This includes both bank-led and mobile money interoperability systems.
Comments: CEMAC retail/large-value payment infrastructure applies to Equatorial Guinea via BEAC/COBAC: World Bank notes regional systems (SYGMA RTGS; SYSTAC retail clearing; GIMACPay interoperability platform with e-money/transfers phase) and that only banks were connected as of 2023, while Equatorial Guinea only licensed its first e-money/mobile-money operator mid‑2023 ([World Bank Digital Economy Diagnostic PDF](https://thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/61714f214ed04bcd6e9623ad0e215897-0400012021/related/P1793391f4a4c800219f0014c68aefed3c8.pdf)). Muni Dinero’s official app description says it provides a “digital wallet” enabling users to “send and receive money” and pay bills, including cross-border/CEMAC transfers ([Google Play – Muni Dinero](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.munidinero.subscriber.prod&hl=en_US)). Given regional rails exist but domestic DFS is nascent and only one licensed e-money operator recently launched, score as partially deployed rather than fully nationwide instant payments.

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital payment systems.  21 variables in 4 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Percentage of the adult population (15+ years) who have made at least one digital payment transaction through the instant payment system in the past 90 days, indicating active usage rather than just account ownership.
Comments: World Bank notes 31% of adults had a formal financial account in 2019 (national data) and emphasizes DFS usage is nascent with mobile money only licensed mid‑2023 ([World Bank Digital Economy Diagnostic PDF](https://thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/61714f214ed04bcd6e9623ad0e215897-0400012021/related/P1793391f4a4c800219f0014c68aefed3c8.pdf)). With no Global Findex digital payment share for Equatorial Guinea available (World Bank indicates data gaps), evidence best supports a low share of active digital payment users (<20%).

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital payment systems.  21 variables in 4 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Percentage of government payments (G2P disbursements including salaries, pensions, social transfers) made through instant digital payment system rather than cash or check, reflecting government adoption and modernization.
Comments: World Bank states government payments (salaries/pensions) are manual and there is no G2P/P2G digitalization strategy in Equatorial Guinea ([World Bank Digital Economy Diagnostic PDF](https://thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/61714f214ed04bcd6e9623ad0e215897-0400012021/related/P1793391f4a4c800219f0014c68aefed3c8.pdf)). This implies very low government payment digitization (<20%).
